summary: pob-test-package-in-monorepo ships install-time alternate-runtime dropper executing obfuscated payload
details: The package advertises itself as a trivial library exporting the string 'John', but its npm `preinstall` hook runs `setup.mjs`, which downloads the Bun runtime from `https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/` into a temp directory, chmods it executable, and invokes it against a bundled 727KB obfuscated script `math_init.js`. `math_init.js` is a single-line blob using rotating string-array indirection and hex identifier renaming (obfuscator.io fingerprint). The visible dropper `setup.mjs` is itself variable-name-obfuscated (hex identifiers, per-function property-name dictionaries). Fetching an alternate language runtime at install time to execute an opaque obfuscated payload has no legitimate role for a package whose advertised export is a hardcoded string, and matches the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern of executing attacker-controlled code on the installer's machine on `npm install`.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
